slices.label: Men outside the South
slices.source: 1840 census (Sixth Census), free white men aged 20 and over (its nearest bracket to 21+) outside the eleven later-Confederate states; property and taxpaying tests had largely gone (Rhode Island kept a freehold test) and a few New England states let free Black men vote; calibrated to certified returns.

slices.label: Women outside the South
slices.source: No women could vote for president in 1840; the 1840 census count of women aged 20 and over is shown for population only.

slices.label: White Southerners
slices.source: 1840 census, free white adults (20+) in the eleven later-Confederate states; white men voted, except that South Carolina's legislature chose its electors; calibrated to certified returns.

slices.label: Black Southerners, most of them enslaved
slices.source: 1840 census, Black adults in the eleven later-Confederate states, overwhelmingly enslaved; enslaved people could not vote, and every Southern state had barred free Black men from voting by 1840 (Tennessee 1834, North Carolina 1835).

slices.label: Immigrants not yet citizens
slices.source: Estimate only: the census did not record nativity before 1850, so the foreign-born count is back-projected from the 1850 census and arrival records; naturalized immigrant men (five years' residence) could vote, aliens could not.

whatIfs.label: Everyone Votes
whatIfs.detail: Every adult can vote, and turns out.
whatIfs.assumption: Every adult votes. Non-citizens choose like naturalized citizens of their state and sex; Black Southerners like Black voters outside the South; everyone else as their group did in 1840.

runs.summary: Rerun with nothing changed, 1840 comes out as it did: Harrison wins, 234–60. The closest state was Pennsylvania, which went to Harrison by 0.1 points. Every one of my 100 reruns reproduces it exactly.
howIGotThis: The numbers: the 1840 census counts and certified returns; every draw reproduces 1840 exactly before the change.
How sure: I reran it 100 times with different population and parameter draws.

everyone.summary: 6.3 million more adults vote. Van Buren wins, 102–192. The closest call is Tennessee, which holds for Harrison by 2.3 points. Van Buren wins in 91 of 100 draws.
assumptions: Every adult votes. Non-citizens choose like naturalized citizens of their state and sex; Black Southerners like Black voters outside the South; everyone else as their group did in 1840.
howIGotThis: What changed: Every adult can vote, and turns out.
New voters borrow the behaviour of naturalized citizens of the same state and sex; Black voters outside the South.

How sure: I reran it 100 times with different population and parameter draws.

south-white.name: Anna Reed
south-white.quote: I cannot vote, though I hear much talk of the election. My husband and his brother debate the banking question at table most evenings.
south-white.controlQuote: I cannot vote, though I hear much talk of the election. My husband and his brother debate the banking question at table most evenings.

women.name: Ruth Robinson
women.quote: I cannot vote myself, being a woman, but my husband will decide how our household votes come election day.
women.controlQuote: I cannot vote myself, being a woman, but my husband will decide how our household votes come election day.

men.name: Ernest Reed
men.quote: The times have been hard since '37, and this General promises work and fair wages again. The bank and currency troubles have hurt us working men too much.
